entities.summary: Álvaro de Sande was a Spanish nobleman and military leader who played a key role in the Spanish Empire's expansion into the New World. He was a skilled diplomat and strategist, known for his ability to navigate the complex web of alliances and rivalries between European powers. De Sande's military campaigns in the Americas helped to establish Spain as a dominant force in the region, and his legacy continued to shape Spanish foreign policy for centuries to come. His experiences in the New World also had a profound impact on his own worldview, as he struggled to reconcile the harsh realities of colonialism with his own sense of nobility and duty. This tension is reflected in the works of the Spanish poet and historian, Luis de Góngora, who wrote about de Sande's exploits in his book, 'Soledad del Amor' (Solitude of Love).
